name: Grade 7 IT: Movement, Sensors, and Feedback
description: Controlled motion, speed, timing, calibration, LEDs, sound signals, ultrasonic readings, thresholds, and if/else reactions.

words.definition: A robot action that changes position or direction.
words.example: The movement command made the robot turn.
Higher speed made the robot travel farther.
The robot moved for two seconds.

words.definition: How far apart two points or objects are.
words.example: The sensor measured the distance to the wall.

words.definition: The way something moves or faces.
words.example: The route changed direction at the turn.

words.definition: Adjusting values so behavior becomes more accurate.
words.example: Calibration helped the robot turn 90 degrees.

words.definition: How close a result is to the intended result.
words.example: The robot needed better accuracy on the square path.
The sequence was forward, turn, forward, stop.

words.definition: The current mode or condition of a robot.
A light, sound, or message that communicates information.
words.example: The buzzer signal meant the robot had stopped.
The LED pattern showed movement and stop states.

words.definition: Using high-frequency sound to measure distance.
words.example: The ultrasonic sensor detected nearby objects.

words.definition: A value measured by a sensor.
words.example: The sensor reading changed when the object moved closer.

words.definition: A limit value used to make a decision.
words.example: A threshold of 10 cm meant too close.

words.definition: A rule that can be true or false.
words.example: The condition checked if the object was close.

words.definition: A programming word that starts a condition.
words.example: If the object is close, the robot stops.

words.definition: The action that happens when an if condition is false.
Able to respond to input or changes.
words.example: A reactive robot stopped when it saw an obstacle.
